headline: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics resolve tumor niches linked to immune exclusion
label: Single Cell Spatial Transcriptomics
summary: Spatial and single-cell profiling now places tumor and stromal programs within tissue niches, linking them to immune exclusion and therapy response.
synthesis: The dominant thread is pairing single-cell RNA-seq with spatial or bulk transcriptomic context to resolve which cell states carry tumor-relevant programs. Spatial transcriptomics anchors these states in tissue: spatial profiling of ICB-treated NSCLC links CD8+ T-cell exclusion to reduced tumor antigen-presentation genes and myofibroblastic CAF stromal programs, while MIBI spatial proteomics in PDAC maps immune cell neighborhoods and immunosuppressive myeloid enrichment at tumor-immune interfaces. Decoder-FFPE-seq extends spatial transcriptomics to archival FFPE tissue at single-cell resolution. Other items rely on scRNA-seq with CellChat or deconvolution, such as lactate-driven reprogramming in colorectal liver metastasis and AML signaling networks, or on bulk data with survival modelling. What is new is spatial placement of niche-level programs within immune remodeling and treatment context, though these associations remain correlative.
